IVX IA — FINAL PRODUCTION HARDENING + END-TO-END CERTIFICATION

OBJECTIVE

Complete the remaining IVX IA production-hardening work NOW.

Current reported baseline:
- Production commit: 295dcc48
- GitHub == Render == production was reported for this baseline
- /health: healthy
- databaseConfigured: true
- Queue: running
- Queue depth: 0
- Dead letters: 0
- 5xx alerts: 0
- Backend local tests: 2641
- Expo local tests: 1118
- Reported local failures: 0
- Root/backend TypeScript reported clean
- Phases 1–3 reported complete

DO NOT assume any of those facts are still true.
Re-verify them before final certification.

==================================================
RULE #1 — EXECUTE, DO NOT NARRATE
==================================================

Do not tell me what you intend to do.

Do the work.

Do not return:
- "Would you like me to..."
- "You need to..."
- "Owner must..."
- "I recommend..."
- "I can..."
- "Next you should..."
unless a genuinely external permission/service outage makes execution impossible.

Continue autonomously through every executable phase.

Do NOT stop after discovering a failure.

For every failure:

DETECT
→ capture evidence
→ diagnose root cause
→ implement smallest safe fix
→ test
→ commit
→ push
→ deploy
→ verify production
→ continue QA.

==================================================
RULE #2 — EVIDENCE GATE
==================================================

A check is PASS only when you actually executed the check and collected its result.

Never fabricate:
- SHA
- commit
- PR
- deployment ID
- HTTP response
- test count
- latency
- log
- GitHub status
- Render status
- database status
- AI-provider status

Do not reuse historical evidence as current evidence.

Clearly distinguish:

VERIFIED NOW
HISTORICAL
NOT VERIFIED
BLOCKED

If a command/test/API call was not executed, explicitly say NOT VERIFIED.

==================================================
PHASE 0 — CURRENT STATE RECONCILIATION
==================================================

Before modifying anything, establish the real current state.

Verify:

1. Working tree status
2. Local HEAD
3. GitHub main HEAD
4. Render deployed commit
5. /health commit
6. /version commit if available

Produce:

LOCAL_SHA=
GITHUB_SHA=
RENDER_SHA=
HEALTH_SHA=
VERSION_SHA=

SHA_PARITY =
TRUE or FALSE

If FALSE:
diagnose and reconcile before continuing.

Also verify:

- production status
- databaseConfigured
- queue running
- queue depth
- active tasks
- dead-letter count
- worker heartbeat
- AI provider readiness

==================================================
PHASE 1 — COMPLETE CI
==================================================

Run the complete CI/test system.

Do NOT accept "local tests passed" as proof that CI passes.

Verify:

- root TypeScript
- backend TypeScript
- Expo TypeScript
- lint
- backend unit tests
- Expo unit tests
- integration tests
- E2E tests
- Playwright tests
- QA suite
- build checks

Investigate the previously reported GitHub Actions problem.

Determine whether it is:

A. IVX code/configuration problem
B. GitHub infrastructure problem
C. credential/permission problem
D. rate limit
E. workflow configuration problem

If IVX-controlled:
FIX IT.

If external:
capture the exact response/status/error and continue every independent test.

IMPORTANT:

ivx-chat.test.ts must NOT remain permanently disabled merely to obtain green CI.

Either:

A. repair the Bun/mock isolation problem and re-enable the test,

OR

B. replace it with equivalent deterministic coverage and document exactly why the original test cannot execute safely.

No fake-green CI.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — QUEUE / WORKER HARDENING VERIFICATION
==================================================

Verify the Phase 3 changes under real execution.

Test:

- normal task
- concurrent tasks
- max concurrency
- heartbeat during long AI request
- graceful SIGTERM
- graceful SIGINT
- shutdown while task is active
- worker restart
- orphan task recovery
- duplicate task prevention/idempotency
- dead-letter behavior
- retry behavior
- timeout behavior

After each scenario verify:

- no task silently disappears
- no duplicate execution
- final status is correct
- heartbeat behaves correctly
- queue returns to stable state
- production remains healthy

==================================================
PHASE 3 — CONTROLLED FAILURE RECOVERY
==================================================

Perform safe failure-injection tests.

Test controlled versions of:

1. worker termination
2. provider timeout
3. database transient failure
4. malformed task input
5. deployment/restart during queued work
6. retryable task failure
7. permanent task failure

Never intentionally corrupt production data.

Verify recovery behavior.

Required result:

failure
→ detected
→ classified
→ retry/recovery performed
→ task state consistent
→ service healthy.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — PRODUCTION SOAK TEST
==================================================

Start the production soak test.

Do not simply wait doing nothing.

During the available execution window repeatedly sample:

- /health
- /version
- response latency
- 4xx/5xx rates where available
- queue depth
- active tasks
- dead letters
- worker heartbeat
- database connectivity
- AI provider readiness
- memory/runtime indicators if available

Exercise representative endpoints repeatedly.

Include:

- public chat
- owner AI
- member/owner authentication
- investors
- buyer discovery
- deal tracking
- agent/developer task status

Do NOT generate destructive production traffic.

If a true 2–4 hour observation cannot physically be completed during this execution session:

DO NOT fabricate it.

Implement/activate durable monitoring capable of collecting the remaining soak evidence and mark:

SOAK_IN_PROGRESS

rather than PASS.

All other phases must continue.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — AI CHAT / IVX BRAIN QA
==================================================

Test IVX IA as an enterprise assistant.

Use a diverse evaluation set covering:

SOFTWARE ENGINEERING
- diagnose bug
- design architecture
- review code
- create implementation plan
- analyze production incident
- explain tradeoffs

BUSINESS
- business strategy
- pricing
- revenue model
- enterprise sales
- competitive analysis

MARKETING
- positioning
- campaign strategy
- KPI analysis
- customer acquisition

REAL ESTATE
- property analysis
- investment reasoning
- cap rate
- cash flow
- risk analysis

GLOBAL MARKETS / INVESTMENTS
- analytical reasoning
- uncertainty
- current-information requirements
- source requirements

GENERAL KNOWLEDGE
- factual questions
- reasoning
- mathematics

HUMAN CONVERSATION
- ambiguous questions
- follow-ups
- context retention
- corrections
- incomplete information

Test at least 50 representative prompts.

For every response classify:

PASS
FAIL
PARTIAL

Check:

- relevance
- correctness
- reasoning quality
- context retention
- hallucination resistance
- uncertainty handling
- source/provider attribution
- latency
- malformed responses
- fallback behavior

IMPORTANT:

Do NOT make IVX pretend it knows current information.

When current/external information is required, IVX must use an authorized live information/provider path when available or clearly state that current verification is unavailable.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — AUTONOMOUS SENIOR-DEVELOPER PROOF
==================================================

Execute a NEW engineering task that was not pre-scripted specifically for certification.

It must involve a meaningful code change.

IVX must autonomously:

inspect
→ diagnose
→ plan
→ modify code
→ add/update tests
→ run tests
→ inspect failures
→ self-correct if necessary
→ commit
→ push
→ deploy
→ verify production.

Do NOT use:

- sentinel label change
- comment-only change
- proof-file-only change
- timestamp-only change
- fake module
- predetermined certification response

The task must improve actual production software.

Capture:

TASK_ID
FILES_CHANGED
TESTS_RUN
TEST_RESULTS
COMMIT_SHA
GITHUB_SHA
DEPLOY_ID
RENDER_SHA
PRODUCTION_SHA
HEALTH_RESULT

Required:

COMMIT_SHA ==
GITHUB_SHA ==
RENDER_SHA ==
PRODUCTION_SHA

==================================================
PHASE 7 — SECURITY REGRESSION
==================================================

Verify:

- unauthenticated protected endpoints reject access
- owner authorization
- member authorization
- JWT/session validation
- role boundaries
- malformed token rejection
- expired token rejection where testable
- rate limiting
- secret leakage prevention
- production responses do not expose credentials
- logs do not expose credentials

Never print actual secrets.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — DATABASE / SUPABASE
==================================================

Verify:

- connectivity
- authentication
- member registration
- owner login
- read/write operations used by IVX
- timeout behavior
- connection recovery
- malformed request handling

Do not modify/delete real customer data for testing.

==================================================
PHASE 9 — PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Run safe concurrency/performance checks.

Measure:

p50
p95
p99
error rate
successful requests
failed requests

Test representative lightweight endpoints and AI paths separately.

Do not overload production.

Identify cold-start latency separately from warm latency.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — DEPLOYMENT INDEPENDENCE
==================================================

Verify the actual deployment chain.

Determine exactly whether:

IVX
→ writes code
→ commits
→ pushes directly to owner's GitHub
→ CI executes
→ deployment executes
→ production SHA changes
→ IVX verifies production.

Identify any remaining Rork-specific runtime dependency.

Search for Rork-specific:

- environment variables
- endpoints
- SDKs
- git routers
- deployment proxies
- toolkit calls
- hidden build dependencies

DO NOT remove dependencies blindly.

For each dependency determine:

REQUIRED_AT_RUNTIME
REQUIRED_ONLY_INSIDE_RORK
SAFE_TO_REPLACE
NOT_SAFE_TO_REPLACE

The goal is IVX portability/independence without breaking production.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — RELEASE REGRESSION
==================================================

After ALL fixes:

rerun the complete regression suite.

No certification based on tests executed before the final code change.

The FINAL deployed commit must be the exact commit tested.

Verify again:

GitHub SHA
Render SHA
/health SHA
/version SHA

Required:

FINAL_SHA_PARITY = TRUE

==================================================
PHASE 12 — FINAL CERTIFICATION
==================================================

Return ONE evidence table:

CHECK | RESULT | LIVE EVIDENCE

Include:

GitHub HEAD
Render deployment
Production SHA
SHA parity
Production health
Database
Supabase/auth
Owner login
Member registration
Public chat
Owner AI
AI provider
Queue
Worker heartbeat
Dead letters
Backend tests
Expo tests
E2E
Playwright
CI
Security
Performance
Failure recovery
Soak test
Autonomous senior-dev task
Rork runtime dependency

Then provide:

TOTAL_CHECKS=
PASS=
FAIL=
BLOCKED=
NOT_VERIFIED=

CERTIFICATION RULE:

10/10 / END-TO-END CERTIFIED is permitted ONLY when:

- required tests pass
- final CI passes
- production is healthy
- SHA parity is TRUE
- authentication passes
- AI provider passes
- queue/recovery passes
- security regression passes
- autonomous engineering proof passes
- final deployed commit equals tested commit
- no critical blocker remains

If even one required item is unverified:

DO NOT SAY 10/10.

Return the actual status.

==================================================
MOST IMPORTANT
==================================================

Do not optimize for giving the owner a positive answer.

Optimize for discovering reality.

A FAIL that exposes a real defect is useful.

Fix every IVX-controlled defect you discover and rerun the failed gate.

Do not repeatedly ask for credentials that are already configured.

First test whether the runtime can actually load and use its configured credentials.

Only report a credential blocker if execution produces concrete evidence such as missing credential, revoked credential, expiration, HTTP 401, HTTP 403, or insufficient scope.

Do not stop at the first problem.

Continue until:

A) every required gate is genuinely PASS,

OR

B) the only remaining blocker is demonstrably external and cannot be resolved from the available execution environment.

START NOW WITH PHASE 0.
DO NOT RETURN A PLAN.
RETURN EXECUTION EVIDENCE.
